title: Power Update After K-th Largest Insertion I
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer p, for each query insert a value into nums, find the ki-th largest element, update p to p^x modulo 10^9 + 7, and return the final p value for each query.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer p, for each query insert a value into nums, find the ki-th largest element, update p to p^x modulo 10^9 + 7, and return the final p value for each query.
constraints: nums and queries are nonempty; values and p are positive.
Each query inserts its value, then selects the kth largest current element; consecutive k values differ by less than ten.
Return p after every sequential update modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Keep exactly k largest values in one heap after each query.
Use a min-heap for those k values and a max-heap for everything smaller.
Insert relative to the current boundary, then move heap roots until the upper heap has the new requested size k.
The upper minimum is the kth largest; the small change in consecutive k values keeps rebalancing limited.
editorial: The upper minimum is the kth largest; the small change in consecutive k values keeps rebalancing limited.

tests.explanation: The selected exponents are three and two, so the running powers are 64 and 4096.
Rebalancing around k selects four for the first query and seven for the second.
